title: Staged admittance policy templater for phased model introductions
creator: Lena Zhang
description: Implement a reusable policy templater and runtime contract for staged model introductions (canary/A-B/shadow modes) that lets platform users declare traffic choreography, step scheduling, metric guardrails, and automated rollback conditions. The goal is a compact declarative surface that teams can use in hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so rollout behavior is consistent across environments. This ticket covers design and an initial implementation of the templater, integration points for telemetry and alerting, and a test harness for simulation and e2e verification.
acceptance_criteria: A declarative policy schema (v1) supports: traffic fractions per step, step durations, pause points with manual approval, shadow-only targets, and explicit fallback variants
Runtime can compile a policy into a deterministic execution plan and expose a plan preview API in the Console
Guardrails: latency, error-rate, and model-quality regression checks are configurable per-policy and enforceable at runtime
Rollback triggers: automatic rollback when configured thresholds breach for an evaluation window; rollback is logged and emits a console event and incident ticket link
Simulator: a workload simulator validates policy behavior against synthetic traffic and emits a summary report; run included in CI
Docs: design doc, example policies for canary, A/B, and shadow testing, and Console UI mock for policy editor
updates: 2025-02-19 - Lena Zhang: Kickoff meeting with PM and SRE. Agreed scope: templater + runtime compiler + simulator. Decided to keep schema minimal for v1; heavy feature parity to follow in v2.
2025-02-24 - Miguel Torres: Prototype policy schema (see links) implemented. Basic compile pipeline converts declarative policy into step timeline and traffic rules. Initial unit tests added.

2025-02-27 - Asha Patel (PM): Reviewed initial schema; requested explicit shadow-only mode and clearer semantics for 'pause' steps vs 'monitor' steps. Added acceptance criteria for plan preview in Console.

2025-03-03 - Miguel Torres: Integrated with telemetry adapter. Proof-of-concept: policy emits step-level metrics to /metrics and creates SLO-bound events. Found an edge case around multi-region fallback; created ENG-942581 to track follow-up.

2025-03-04 - Design review notes: Use percentage-based traffic routing for first two steps, then switch to cohort-based routing for A/B. We will add a 'safety-multiplier' config to lengthen evaluation windows for low-traffic workloads.
notes: Decision: Keep v1 schema explicit and opinionated rather than attempting to support a Turing-complete DSL. Helps with validation and security review in Private deployments.

Trade-off: Cohort-based routing requires user-provided stable keys. For PLG users we'll expose a simple cookie-based cohort generator but recommend server-side cohort assignment for production tenants.
Risk: Automatic rollback semantics must be conservative; SRE asked for an optional cool-down window before automated rollback to avoid flip-flopping during transient spikes.
Follow-up: Add cryptographic signing for policy artifacts deployed to Private control planes (security review required in later sprint).
